title: Grateful Dead Live at Strand Lyceum on 1972-05-26
source: Master SBD reel > DAT > CD-R >EAC > CDR

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of the May 26 1972 show with a monster first set and an epic Truckin’/The Other One suite featuring soaring Garcia and stellar Keith work.
ai_review.review: Reviewers rave about the pristine, full‑spectrum soundboard tape – calling it the best circulating version with virtually no patches or muffiness. Musically the concert is described as monumental: a blistering first set highlighted by Cumberland Blues, Jack Straw, China > Rider and an extended Playin’ in the Band, followed by a second‑set marathon of Truckin’, The Other One (35+ minutes) and a breathtaking Morning Dew Prelude jam. Energy is consistently high and every band member receives praise, especially Keith’s keyboard wizardry and Garcia’s soaring leads.

ai_rating.rationale: All five reviews award 5 stars, emphasizing both an outstanding performance and near‑perfect soundboard quality; the consistency and detail across multiple reviewers justify a top‑tier rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Described as crystal clear, full spectrum, with no noticeable patches. Minor cuts/blips are mentioned but do not detract from overall clarity; one tape flip in the Dew is noted.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A monster 19‑song first set flows seamlessly into a second set that opens with an extended jam suite, culminating in the legendary Truckin’/The Other One marathon and a transcendent Morning Dew finale.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is praised as soaring and perfectly locked in with Keith; his leads are described as 'smoking' and 'tight'.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass solo before The Other One intro is highlighted, and his counterpoint work during the Prelude jam receives commendation.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob contributes solid rhythm and counterpoint throughout; reviewers note his interplay with Garcia and Phil.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s playing is called extraordinary—creating themes out of nothing, sounding like Steve Winwood, and delivering the most compelling keyboard moments of the night.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum solo after The Other One intro is noted as great, supporting the high‑energy flow of the second set.
